Bullish Engulfing

Yutan Boğa

A reversal pattern that forms after a decline, when a large green candle completely engulfs the body of the previous red candle. It can signal that selling pressure is fading and buyers are starting to take control.

How it forms

  • It follows a clear decline. Since it is a reversal signal, there needs to be a move to reverse.
  • Candle 1 is red: it closes below its open.
  • Candle 2 is green: it closes above its open.
  • The body of candle 2 completely covers the body of candle 1: it opens at or below candle 1's close and closes above candle 1's open.

Crypto trades 24/7, so gaps between candles are rare. Candle 2 usually opens exactly at candle 1's close. This does not invalidate the pattern.

What it suggests

The first candle shows sellers are still in control. The second candle, over the same length of time, takes back all of the sellers' gains and closes above them. This suggests the balance may be starting to shift in favour of buyers.

On its own, the pattern does not prove that the direction has changed. Read it as a hint that the decline is slowing, and weigh it together with other evidence.

When it strengthens, when it weakens

Strengthens

  • Forming at a support zone
  • A clear decline before the pattern
  • High volume on candle 2
  • Candle 2 also covering candle 1's wicks
  • Forming on a higher timeframe (4H, 1D)

Weakens

  • Forming in a flat, directionless market
  • Both candles being very small
  • Low volume
  • A strong resistance zone just above
  • Forming on very low timeframes (1m, 5m)

The MarketLevelMap view

How it relates to zones

Bullish engulfing candles are common and often mean little. Where they really stand out is when price reaches a support zone. The zone marks an area where price has reacted before; the pattern can show buyers stepping back in at that area. Together they paint a more meaningful picture than either does alone.

The reverse also holds: a bullish engulfing that forms just below a resistance zone is considered weaker, because sellers are waiting overhead.

When it is invalidated

If price closes below the pattern's lowest point (including both candles' wicks), the bullish scenario is considered invalid. If the pattern formed at a support zone, a close below the zone means the same.

Knowing the invalidation point in advance is the clearest way to tell when the pattern no longer says anything.

Often confused with

  • Bearish EngulfingThe opposite: after a rise, a red candle engulfs the green one.
  • Piercing LineThe green candle closes past the middle of the red body but does not cover all of it.
  • Bullish HaramiThe inverse relationship: a small green candle sits inside a large red body.
